parts.label: a
parts.technique: Conservation of linear momentum / collision
parts.reason: This requires the principle of conservation of linear momentum (CLM) applied to a direct collision between two particles. No statement in the given list covers momentum, impulse or collisions (M6-M9 statements cover units, kinematics, forces/Newton's laws, and moments only - no momentum/impulse section exists).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Impulse-momentum equation
parts.reason: Impulse = change in momentum is not covered by any listed statement; no momentum/impulse topic present in the M6-M9 statements given.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Direction of impulse
parts.reason: Depends on the out-of-spec impulse calculation in (b); also impulse itself is not a listed topic.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat, motion under gravity
parts.reason: Vertical motion under gravity using constant acceleration formulae is covered by M7.3 (constant acceleration formulae) with M8.3 (motion under gravity, constant g).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat, speed before impact
parts.reason: Uses v^2=u^2+2as, a standard constant acceleration formula, covered by M7.3/M8.3.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: suvat, total distance travelled (up and down)
parts.reason: Finding distances via suvat for upward and downward legs is standard M7.3/M7.1 (distance travelled) application.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: velocity-time graph sketching
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers velocity-time graphs and their interpretation, including sketching for constant acceleration motion.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Resolving forces perpendicular to inclined plane
parts.reason: Finding normal reaction on inclined plane by resolving forces is covered by M8.4 guidance (resolving on inclined plane).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Friction (limiting), F <= muR, equilibrium on inclined plane
parts.reason: Explicitly covered by M8.6 (F <= muR model, limiting friction, statics) combined with M8.4 resolving on inclined plane.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Friction (limiting), least force in equilibrium
parts.reason: Same as above, use of limiting friction model in equilibrium, M8.6.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Moments of a non-uniform rod, tipping point conditions
parts.reason: Directly matches M9.1 'Understand and use moments in simple static contexts', including tipping/tilting problems with non-uniform rods.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Vector magnitude (speed) at a given time
parts.reason: Finding speed from a velocity vector at a specific time uses vector magnitude (P10.2) combined with kinematics of a particle moving with constant acceleration in 2D (M7.3).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Angle between vector and direction using trig
parts.reason: Finding angle of a velocity vector using tan, within 2D vector kinematics context, covered by M7.3 extension to vectors and P10 vector work.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding constant acceleration vector by differentiation or from velocity equation
parts.reason: M7.4 explicitly covers use of calculus (differentiation) in kinematics extended to 2 dimensions using vectors, matching the mark scheme's differentiation approach; alternative method using v=u+at also matches M7.3.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Finding time when velocity is parallel to a given direction vector
parts.reason: Uses ratio of vector components for parallel direction, within 2D vector kinematics context covered by M7.3 (motion in 2D using vectors) and P10 vectors (parallel vectors).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Newton's second law for connected particles on inclined plane
parts.reason: Matches M8.4 guidance explicitly: 'Problems may be set where forces need to be resolved, e.g. at least one of the particles is moving on an inclined plane' for connected particles (rigid coupling, thrust).

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law, finding driving force D
parts.reason: Same connected-particle/inclined-plane N2L context as (a), covered by M8.2/M8.4.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Connected particles over a smooth pulley, tension, force on pulley
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly states 'application to problems involving smooth pulleys and connected particles', matching this exact scenario.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Explaining use of 'smooth pulley' assumption (equal tension)
parts.reason: This is a direct consequence of the smooth pulley model explicitly named in M8.4's guidance; understanding that tension is equal on both sides due to smoothness is part of applying that model.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding distance from acceleration-time graph (area under a-t graph)
parts.reason: M7.4 explicitly gives v=integral of a dt, and area under an acceleration-time graph is the integral of acceleration, i.e. the change in velocity; converting this then to distance uses v-t graph area (M7.2). Though a-t graphs are not explicitly named in M7.2, the calculus-based justification (M7.4) supports it as an alternative in-spec method.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Total distance from acceleration-time graph via velocities and trapezium areas under v-t graph
parts.reason: Same reasoning as (a): using areas under the acceleration-time graph to find velocities (M7.4, integration) then areas under implied velocity-time graph (trapezium) for distance (M7.2).
